test_title: SSC CPO 2023 Official Paper-I (Held On: 04 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Who explained the structure of protein?
solution:
The Correct Answer is **__Pauling and Corey__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Linus Pauling** is recognized for successfully predicting regular **protein secondary structures **based on** hydrogen bonding,** an idea originally proposed by **William Astbury**.
 
• **Pauling and Corey** formulated a model for the conformation of **fibrous proteins called beta-keratins**, where the polypeptide adopts an extended zig-zag configuration rather than a coil, such as in the alpha-helix.
 
• All proteins in the human body can be synthesized from permutations of just **20 amino acids**.
 
• There are seven primary types of proteins: antibodies, contractile proteins, enzymes, hormonal proteins, structural proteins, storage proteins, and transport proteins.
 
• A protein molecule is composed of a lengthy chain of these amino acids, each linked to its adjacent amino acid through a covalent peptide bond.
 
• Hence, proteins are also referred to as polypeptides. Each type of protein possesses a distinctive sequence of amino acids, which remains identical from one molecule to another.
 
• Numerous proteins with diverse functions are known, each characterized by its specific amino acid sequence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Emil Fischer**, a German organic chemist, is credited with the** discovery of caffeine **and other related purines.
 
• Additionally, he conducted extensive research on the molecular structures of sugars and proteins, earning him the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1902.
 
• **Proteins** are comprised of amino acids, with **21 naturally occurring variants**.
 
• Secondary protein structures are stabilized by hydrogen bonding. The characteristics of protein strands vary depending on the type of hydrogen bonding present, with two common types being the alpha helix and beta sheet.
 
• The alpha helix is a right-handed coiled secondary protein structure, where the substituents of the amino acids extend outward.
 
• Hydrogen bonds form between the carbonyl oxygen and the four NH bonds below it, contributing to the stability of the helix.
